 Tigers' tricky equation for final
 Published : 20 October 2026
 • 
 Updated : 21 October 2026, 14:47
 • 
 CRICKET
 SHARE 
 Sports Reporter 
 Photo: BCB 
 Bangladesh face an uphill task to keep their UAE ODI Tri-Series final hopes alive after a crushing 99-run defeat in their tournament opener.  
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 Read more What to watch on TV today (21 Oct, 2026) 
 Heading into Wednesday's must-win clash against Afghanistan at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium, simply securing a victory will not be enough for the Tigers. Locked in a net run rate battle with Zimbabwe for the apparent second spot in Friday's final, Bangladesh must hit specific mathematical targets to advance. 
 Read more ‘We must play our brand of top-class cricket’ 
 If Bangladesh bat first 
 If Bangladesh score 235 or less, they must win by 41 runs to move ahead on NRR.
 If Bangladesh score 236 or more, a 40-run win is enough (as Bangladesh would edge out Zimbabwe on higher overall tournament scoring rate).
 Read more Tigers must win big against Afghanistan and overcome NRR mountain to reach tri-series final 
 If Bangladesh bat second 
 Chasing 201 (if AFG score 200): Must win inside 40.3 overs (or 41.1 overs if finishing with a boundary when scores are level).
 Chasing 251 (if AFG score 250): Must win inside 41.3 overs (or 42.1 overs if finishing with a boundary when scores are level).
 Chasing 301 (if AFG score 300): Must win inside 42.2 overs (or 43.0 overs if finishing with a boundary when scores are level).
 Read more Can Tigers’ middle order bat smarter? 
 ***Boasting a massive +3.160 NRR, Afghanistan will reach Friday's final unless they suffer a massive defeat (losing by 129+ runs or inside ~16.5 overs), which would put Bangladesh and Zimbabwe through. Conversely, Zimbabwe advances alongside Afghanistan if the Afghans win, or if Bangladesh wins by less than the required 41-run or ~41-over margin.
